title: PBQ 1 — parted HOTSPOT
desc: A new drive (/dev/sdc) was recently added to a Linux system. Complete the following tasks:
tasks: Create an appropriate GPT device label.
Create a primary ext4 partition spanning the disk (1–10G).
Format the new partition with ext4.
inst: Use the drop-down menus to select the correct object for each blank. Some commands are partially complete. Not all objects will be used, and some may be used more than once.
expl:
parted -s /dev/sdc mklabel gpt
  → Creates a GPT (GUID Partition Table) label. -s = script/non-interactive mode.

parted -s /dev/sdc mkpart primary ext4 1 10G
  → Creates a primary partition, ext4 type, from 1MB to 10GB.

mkfs.ext4 /dev/sdc1
  → Formats /dev/sdc1 with the ext4 filesystem.

title: PBQ 2 — LVM Recovery
desc: A junior system administrator removed an LVM (Logical Volume Manager) volume by mistake.
inst: Review the terminal output shown for each part, then select the appropriate command from the dropdown.

parts.label: Part 1
parts.prompt: Select the appropriate command to BEGIN the recovery process.
parts.ctx:
[root@comptiasim ~]# vgs
 VG    #PV #LV #SN Attr   VSize    VFree
 vg01    1   0   0 wz--n- <10.00g <10.00g
parts.ctxLbl: vgs output — vg01 has 0 LVs (the logical volume was accidentally removed):
parts.expl:
vgcfgrestore restores the VG (Volume Group) metadata from the LVM archive.
  -f specifies the archive file (the most recent: _00002)
This recovers the LV definitions that were lost when the admin accidentally removed the volume.

parts.label: Part 2
parts.prompt: Select the appropriate command to CONTINUE the recovery process.
parts.ctxLbl: blkid output — /dev/xvdf is recognised as an LVM2 physical volume:
parts.expl:
lvchange -a y /dev/vg01/lv01 activates the logical volume.
  -a y = activate yes
After restoring the VG metadata, the LV exists in metadata but is inactive (offline). This brings it online so it can be mounted.

parts.label: Part 3
parts.prompt: Select the appropriate command to COMPLETE the recovery and access the data.
parts.ctx:
[root@comptiasim ~]# lsblk
NAME         MAJ:MIN RM SIZE RO TYPE MOUNTPOINT
xvda         202:0    0   8G  0 disk
└─xvda1      202:1    0   8G  0 part /
xvdf         202:88   0  10G  0 disk
└─vg01-lv01  253:0    0   9G  0 lvm
parts.ctxLbl: lsblk output — vg01-lv01 is present and active but has no MOUNTPOINT:
parts.expl:
mount -a mounts all filesystems listed in /etc/fstab.
Since /etc/fstab already has the entry for /dev/vg01/lv01 → /important_data (configured before the accidental removal), mount -a reads that and mounts the now-active LV.

Note: "mount /important_data /dev/vg01/lv01" has reversed arguments — mount expects DEVICE then MOUNTPOINT.

title: PBQ 3 — tar Backup & Restore
desc: You have created an uncompressed backup of the application directory. Several hours later, you must restore the application from backup.
inst: Click tokens to build each command. Click a token in the command bar to remove it. Complete both the Backup and Restore tabs.

tabs.name: Backup
tabs.expl:
tar -cvf /backups/application.tar -C /opt/ application
  -c = create archive
  -v = verbose (list files as processed)
  -f = filename of archive
  -C /opt/ = change directory to /opt/ before archiving
  application = the directory to archive (relative to /opt/)
Produces an uncompressed .tar archive at /backups/application.tar

tabs.name: Restore
tabs.expl:
tar -xvf /backups/application.tar -C /opt/
  -x = extract
  -v = verbose
  -f = filename of archive to extract from
  -C /opt/ = extract into /opt/ directory
Restores /opt/application/ from the backup archive

title: PBQ 4 — Archive Ann → Joe
desc: Joe has taken a position previously held by Ann. Archive all files from Ann's home directory and extract them into Joe's home directory.
inst: Click tokens to build each command. Click a token in the command bar to remove it. Complete both the Archive and Extract tabs.

tabs.name: Archive
tabs.expl:
tar -cvf /tmp/ann.tar -C /home ann
  -c = create  -v = verbose  -f = output file
  -C /home = change to /home/ first
  ann = Ann's directory (relative to /home/)
Creates /tmp/ann.tar containing Ann's home directory

tabs.name: Extract
tabs.expl:
tar -xvf /tmp/ann.tar -C /home/ joe
  -x = extract  -v = verbose  -f = archive file
  -C /home/ = extract into /home/ directory
  joe = extract into Joe's sub-directory
Restores Ann's files into /home/joe/

title: PBQ 1 OLDER — Script Completion
desc: Create a shell script at /tmp/script.sh that finds and compresses rotated log files in /var/log without recursion.
inst: Click a blank to select it (it highlights amber), then click a snippet from the bank to fill it. Click a filled blank to clear and reselect it.
expl:
find /var/log -type f -maxdepth 1 | grep "log.[1-6]$" > /tmp/tempfile
  → Find files (no recursion) in /var/log, filter rotated logs (log.1–log.6), save list.

for filename in $(cat /tmp/tempfile)
do
  gzip $filename
done
  → Loop over each filename and compress it with gzip.

title: PBQ 2 OLDER — Apache httpd
desc: A junior admin had trouble installing and running Apache. Install Apache, start the service, and verify it is running.
inst: Type commands at the prompt. Type "help" to see available commands.

steps.out:
Loaded plugins: fastestmirror
Resolving Dependencies...

Installing:
  httpd.x86_64  2.4.6-97.el7

Complete!

steps.lbl: Enable httpd to start at boot

steps.out:
● httpd.service - The Apache HTTP Server
   Loaded: loaded (/usr/lib/systemd/system/httpd.service; enabled)
   Active: active (running) since Mon 2024-01-15 09:32:01 EDT; 5s ago
 Main PID: 17981 (httpd)

Jan 15 09:32:01 centos7 systemd[1]: Started The Apache HTTP Server.

expl:
1. yum install httpd  → installs Apache HTTP Server
2. systemctl start httpd  → starts the service now
3. systemctl enable httpd  → enables auto-start at boot (the junior admin forgot this step)
4. systemctl status httpd  → confirms Active: (running)

The root cause: Apache was installed and started but not enabled, so it did not survive a reboot.
